title: Routed Continual Learning cost at Hydra's actual prices
method: Parsed data/routing/job-usage-log.jsonl to extract Hydra's actual provider/model call shares and empirical per-call input, cached-input, and output token distributions. Loaded Hydra's pricing schedules from data/prices.json (Vertex Argon 2026-11-12 and 2026-12-01 rates with and without the 50% credit promotion, plus the $0 marginal dollar convention for subscription lanes). Evaluated the 398-instance Routed Continual Learning protocol under (a) the authors' frozen public price schedule (65-72% cost reduction vs one global history) and (b) Hydra's model mix and Vertex Argon rates across homogeneous, cache-asymmetric, and cross-lane (paid router vs $0 subscription executor) regimes, and solved for the router-call break-even point.
assumptions: Protocol and author figures taken verbatim from card C-routed-continual-learning: 398 instances per rollout (301 CL-Bench + 97 tau-bench), 5 matched rollouts, 1 structured-output router call per instance, and 65% to 72% lower estimated API cost for routed full library vs one global history.

Card C-routed-continual-learning reports relative cost percentages (65-72% cheaper than global history; 25-33% cheaper than routed histories on 3 models and +5% on Opus 4.7; +8-29% for single ReasoningBank) and does not print raw per-role token counts or absolute dollar totals.

Pricing convention from data/prices.json: Vertex Argon (google/gemini-4-argon) is priced at $2.00/MTok input, $0.10/MTok cached input, $10.00/MTok output effective 2026-11-12 ($4.00/$0.20/$20.00 from 2026-12-01; 50% credit promotion on net spend). All other Hydra lanes are subscriptions or free tiers carrying $0.00 marginal dollar cost (metered by quota/tokens).

When repricing empirical call footprints from data/routing/job-usage-log.jsonl under Vertex Argon, uncached input tokens are computed as max(0, input_tokens - cached_input_tokens) where cached tokens are logged.

For Vertex prefix-cache sensitivity, we evaluate an illustrative asymmetric cache regime where one global history achieves 80% cached input reuse ($0.10/MTok) and routed clusters achieve 40% cached input reuse due to partition switching.

headline.verdict: Across 13003 logged calls (Vertex Argon share=2.5%, $0 marginal subscription/free share=97.5%), the authors' 65-72% routed-vs-global cost reduction (cost ratio 0.28-0.35) survives at 1.0x in token/quota terms and in homogeneous or uniformly-mixed Vertex Argon dollar runs. Break-even requires additional router overhead equal to 65-72% of global per-instance cost (1.86x-2.57x of total routed cost). Two Hydra-specific caveats can erode or flip the dollar advantage: (1) if global history gets high Vertex prefix-cache reuse (e.g. 80% at $0.10/MTok vs $2.00/MTok uncached) while routed clusters get low reuse (40%), savings shrink from 65-72% to 9.6-27.7%; (2) if execution runs on a $0 marginal-cost subscription lane while the router runs on paid Vertex Argon, marginal dollar cost is higher for routed (398 paid calls vs $0), though the 65-72% quota/token reduction on the subscription lane remains.

hydra_schedule_economics.pricing_convention: Per data/prices.json: Vertex Argon (google/gemini-4-argon) is priced at $2.00/MTok input, $0.10/MTok cached input, $10.00/MTok output effective 2026-11-12 (doubling 2026-12-01; 50% credit promotion available). All other Hydra lanes are subscriptions or free tiers carrying $0.00 marginal dollar cost (metered by quota/tokens).

router_breakeven_analysis.explanation: In single-model or uniformly-mixed rollouts, routed full library saves 65% to 72% of the global history baseline (routed cost is 28% to 35% of global). Thus, the 1 router call per instance would have to add an extra 65% to 72% of the entire per-instance global-history cost (or 1.86x to 2.57x of the total routed per-instance cost) to erase the savings. However, in a split-lane setup where the agent executes on a $0 marginal-cost subscription lane and only the router runs on paid Vertex Argon, global history costs $0.00 marginal USD while routed costs 398 paid router calls, so break-even in marginal dollars is $0.00.
